one_month_reasoning: Corrected from round 1: Avnet's Q1 FY27 report is most likely Wed Nov 4, 2026, outside the window (marked at the Fri Oct 30 close). Q1 ends Oct 3 and every fiscal Q1-Q3 earnings 8-K (Item 2.02) since FY23 Q2 has been filed 32 days after quarter end (EDGAR, source 18); Avnet has not announced the date, and last year it announced 14 days ahead, so a date notice around Oct 21 would confirm. I put ~10% on the print landing inside the window. In-window drivers are only read-throughs (TI and other supplier Q3 reports, memory contract pricing, ECIA/industry sentiment) and macro. I therefore drop my earnings-widened 12% sigma and use a lognormal mix: 85% at 10% monthly sigma and 15% at 16% (fat tails plus the small in-window print chance). The median is $106.3, a touch below spot: the stock ran from ~$88 (Aug 28 Form 4 tax-withholding price) to ~$107 in five weeks to a new high, executives sold into the run at $91-98 (sources 15, 16), and I allow a small short-horizon reversal. This is close to neutral by design.

fair_value.method: Blend of NTM P/E ($11.40 x 9x = $102.6, 40%), normalized through-cycle EPS ($7.60 x 12x = $91, 40%) and price/book on projected Sep-2027 book per diluted share ($66 x 1.6x = $106, 20%), about $99, ~7% below the $106.94 price. Peak-cycle earnings are being capitalised at above-history multiples, but I no longer add a credit-stress discount.

bear.story: Memory price inflation (about a third or more of recent growth) peaks in 2027, customers who built safety stock or double-ordered digest inventory, and sequential sales roll over in H2 FY27. Working-capital burn keeps buybacks off, and the market re-rates to the prior-peak ~6.5x on falling ~$9.5 NTM EPS. Credit is a secondary amplifier here, not the trigger: ratings are investment grade and the market is open.

base.story: The upcycle continues but slows; NTM EPS ~$11.4-11.8, the multiple slips toward ~9x as investors look through to the peak; earnings growth pulls leverage down and buybacks resume in H2 FY27; the stock is roughly flat.

bull.story: The memory/AI-driven shortage runs into 2028, broader component price increases (already emerging per the CFO) add to volume, and mass-market and Western industrial demand recover; EC margins move toward 4.5-5%; EPS run-rate $13-14 at ~10.5x.

thesis_break_reason: ~33% below today and ~6.3x the $11.40 run-rate EPS, i.e. back to prior-peak (FY23) multiples. Trading there would most likely mean evidence the cycle has turned: a sequential guide-down, book-to-bill below 1, memory price reversal or a double-order/inventory unwind. That is not ordinary 37%-vol noise. I keep $72 rather than the supervisor's $70: same rationale, and a slightly earlier trigger suits a skeptic. I dropped the credit-event leg of the round-1 reason, since the August 2026 notes priced at investment grade.

reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor's checks changed three things. (1) Earnings date: Q1 FY27 most likely reports ~Nov 4, outside the 1-month window (32-day 8-K cadence, EDGAR), so I narrowed the 1-month distribution to ~10% sigma plus a fat-tail component. (2) Credit: my round-1 Fitch negative-outlook item was dated 2025 and came from a secondary source. The Aug 19, 2026 FWP for the $550M 5.65% 2031 notes shows Baa3/BBB-/BBB- at T+132bp, a normal investment-grade BBB- spread, and the notes refinance existing debt. I found no current negative rating action. With Q1-guide earnings (~$1.4-1.5B annualised adj operating income) against ~$3.2B gross debt, leverage is falling, not rising. I therefore drop credit stress as a bear trigger and cut bear weight from 25% to 22%. Still skeptical: BBB- is one notch above high yield, so a cyclical downturn plus working-capital debt could bring a downgrade, an amplifier rather than a cause. (3) Memory share of growth: re-sourced to the CFO's call remarks via call highlights (~one-third of Q4 sequential and y/y growth). That confirms rather than overturns my round-1 figure; another forecaster's 'about half' refers to Q3 sequential. (4) Insider selling, re-verified from primary Form 4s: CEO exercised and sold 51,900 shares at $98.46 (Aug 13); GC sold 32,052 at $91.10 (Aug 21); CFO and CIO disposed 6,844 at $92.75 and 13,000 at $93.71 (Sep 15-16); there were no open-market buys. These are mostly option-exercise sales into strength: a mild negative, not a red flag. (5) Diluted share count is ~86M (10-K cover, cash-settled convert principal), which trims my P/B leg from $109 to $106. Fair value moves from $100 to $99 (9x $11.40 NTM; 12x $7.60 normalized; 1.6x $66 book). I still found no short report, litigation or accounting flag; the downside mechanism remains multiple compression as the market anticipates a peak. Scenarios 22/53/25 at $62/$106/$145 give a mean ~$106 and median ~$103. The 12-month ladder is a right-skewed distribution with ~38-40% effective vol, median slightly below spot; it is a point or so higher than round 1 on the left side because the credit tail is smaller. Research was limited to ~8 follow-up queries/fetches; the full transcript was not reachable (503).
